speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information whether the Ministry will require SPH Media Trust to have adequate emphasis on thought leadership content from Singapore’s perspective so as to increase Singapore’s mindshare on the global stage.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information what steps will the Ministry take to ensure that its funding support for SPH Media Trust will go towards the development of news media on online platforms that are engaging for younger audiences.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how will the Ministry ensure that the Singapore Media Academy and the planned SPH Media Academy differentiate themselves in terms of skillsets and avoid an overlap of functions; (b) whether the Ministry has a definite roadmap for SPH’s upcoming media academy to help achieve the goal of nurturing more local talent for the mass communications industry; and (c) whether a collaboration with SG Women In Tech will be considered to attract, retain and develop more female talent in the infocomm workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will also provide more information for written Question No 50 in yesterday's Order Paper, which was filed by Miss Cheryl Chan.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In May last year, Singapore Press Holdings Limited announced the restructuring of its media business to a not-for-profit entity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, the need for Government support for SMT’s transformation; second, how transformation preserves trusted media for our citizens and serves the larger public interest; and third, how the Government will maintain accountability.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Miss Cheryl Chan asked about the Government’s plans to support SMT.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MCI has worked closely with SMT to understand the challenges they face.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, readership and trust in SMT’s journalism continue to be high.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, the global digital shift has severely disrupted print business models.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Traditionally, they have relied heavily on advertising revenue to support quality journalism.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But today, the proliferation of free news aggregators and user-generated content compete with newsrooms for eyeballs and, correspondingly, advertisers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although digital advertising revenue has increased, a large share of it goes to Big Tech platforms like Google and Facebook, or Meta, as it is now known.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On top of the cost of producing quality content, newsrooms must also invest in reaching audiences in a crowded digital space.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In 2019, German publisher Axel Springer committed €100 million in investments for digital growth projects at two of its papers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is on top of its IT development projects supporting its digital business model, which amounted to another €100 million.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The New York Times, prioritising its digital growth, has seen its product development costs increase over 25% year-on-year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The high costs to achieve success online, even for those who already have significant readership, are testament to the challenging industry conditions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As an open, cosmopolitan city-state, we consume varied perspectives from around the world.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nonetheless, preserving our local news media remains critical.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our local news media provide a vital Singaporean lens through which citizens can make sense of global events.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is an essential public good in our multiracial, multi-religious society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In discharging this role, SMT now produces six daily newspapers in four languages.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To achieve its mission, SMT must do three things: first, make long-term investments in the capability development of technology and talent; second, sustain and develop our vernacular news media; and third, position itself as a regional thought leader.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Hany Soh asked about maintaining SMT’s relevance amidst digital disruption, especially for younger audiences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is vital to understand the media consumption habits of our digital native audiences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Based on an MCI survey, around 65% of respondents access SMT’s digital content frequently in 2020.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is a steep jump from about 40% a year before.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In contrast, hardcopy reach declined from about 40% to 30% over the same period, a single year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The digital pivot of SMT will be key to growing its reach with the young and old, and even with overseas audiences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In terms of user experience, digital content must be delivered swiftly, websites must be intuitively designed, applications must allow for personalisation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the newsroom, content management resources, data analytics and investments into artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning tools can help newsrooms push out news quickly, accurately and effectively.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Continual evolution of content forms will also be key.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As with other major publications today, SMT must package complex information in a variety of ways – texts, videos, podcasts and interactive infographics.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is especially important for younger audiences, who demand engaging news they can consume on-the-go.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the backend, infrastructure will have to be robust enough to support the digital transition.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With increasing digital viewership, SMT will also have to ensure resilience and reliability in its news provision.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Hany Soh rightly asked about talent development.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In today’s landscape, the skills required of journalists have changed dramatically.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, beyond covering announcements, journalists have to be data-literate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They need to know when, where and how to reach their digital audiences so that critical news is not buried under masses of information on social media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As part of the transformation, the new SPH Media Academy will update the newsroom’s training programmes for the digital age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They will also partner internationally renowned institutions like the Poynter Institute and the Reuters Institute at Oxford University.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They will offer programmes and fellowships to local journalists.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Ms Hany Soh’s question about external collaborations, SPH Media Academy’s immediate focus will be on equipping its own journalists with digital skills and multimedia capabilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We believe there will be good areas of synergy with the Singapore Media Academy.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will work with Mediacorp and SMT, along with our Institutes of Higher Learning, to promote collaborative efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the long term, SMT can look into extending its programmes to the larger media industry in Singapore and journalists around the region.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The newsrooms will also keep pace with the increasingly complex information landscape.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These initiatives complement the newsrooms’ core strengths, educating readers on identifying misinformation and scams, which are key challenges in today's digital society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked about the viability, relevance and growing the reach of vernacular media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although vernacular readership is smaller and, therefore, much more challenging to independently sustain, it is critical to provide credible news products that serve our multiracial society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He did so because he foresaw that the vernacular press would inevitably come under pressure as English became the language of business, Government and education.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SPH was thus established in 1984 to preserve the Chinese and Malay media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we had allowed our vernacular media to wither, Singapore would have been the poorer for it and we would have lost our souls.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even if they were to be unviable business propositions – which they are not – we believe it is in the public interest to do all we can to preserve and develop all the vernacular outlets in both SMT as well as Mediacorp.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, support from the community is essential to achieve the shared goal of safeguarding our culture and heritage.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this regard, SMT will be partnering clan associations, community groups and schools to provide students with greater access to its vernacular products.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about thought leadership content.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With Singapore’s position as a global hub, SMT is well-placed to provide deep domain knowledge about the region, with a Singapore voice.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To boost its capabilities, SMT will expand its foreign bureaus, host more events and forums and establish more partnerships to build their international audience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, a third of The Straits Times’ readers come from overseas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Zaobao’s websites see around seven million unique visitors monthly, more than half of which are from outside Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Chinese Media Group will be partnering Berita Harian, Tamil Murasu, as well as other media outlets in the region to promote mother tongue language media to a wider audience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As much as the media is coming under challenge throughout the world, we must be mindful that the major powers are waging a constant battle for hearts and minds worldwide – including our hearts and minds in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a small country, we are especially prone to influence campaigns – overt and covert.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And as a multiracial, multilingual country, we are especially prone to the cultural, social and even political influence that countries like China and India can continue to exert abroad.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As open as we must remain to the world, and as welcoming as we are to global media outlets broadcasting and reporting out of Singapore, we must also have Singaporeans reporting on the world from the Singaporean perspective.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A Singaporean reporting on China, for example, would afford us a lens very different from an American or a European doing so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thus, the growth of SMT’s overseas bureaus is an important area of capability development we want to support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During the transition, it will likely be loss-making.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the UK, The Guardian, which has a highly successful digital subscription model with almost a million paying supporters, has lost millions of dollars since 1998.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It only returned to the black in 2019, after years of persistent transformation efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Yet, they still had to cut 12% of their workforce in 2020 to stay afloat.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government is ready to put support behind SMT’s transformation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are committed to safeguarding the information space for our citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Government funding of news media is commonplace in many countries and has increased in some cases during COVID-19.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This underscores the public good that trusted journalism provides in a complex environment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In 2020, the French government introduced a subsidy package of over €480 million to support its news media in weathering COVID-19 losses and moving to digital platforms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the same year, Norway and Sweden rendered €43 million and €65 million of aid respectively to their press.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Prior to its restructuring, Singapore Press Holdings Limited had invested almost $50 million annually in technology and digital talent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This has yielded some success but, from the kind of investments we see elsewhere, they clearly need to do more to accelerate the newsrooms’ transformation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The steep decline of print media and, correspondingly, the migration to the digital space, has brought SMT to an inflection point.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will tap on Government funding to make essential investments that move it decisively into the digital age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will provide SMT with more capital to invest in the future while ensuring that they are able to sustain their current operations during this critical transition period.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The remainder will be spent on newsroom capability building and training, in particular, the vernacular newsrooms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Jessica Tan asked about accountability measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Alex Yam asked how the Ministry will ensure editorial independence continues to be upheld in the newsrooms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT has exercised editorial independence since its establishment in 1984 as Singapore Press Holdings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Funding support does not change that, as is the case with Mediacorp since 2011.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Is such a high level of trust attainable without objective and balanced reporting?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The same report indicated that The Straits Times, one of SMT's flagship products, enjoyed a similarly high level of trust among 77% of respondents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If nobody is reading The Straits Times, Lianhe Zaobao, Berita Harian or Tamil Murasu, if nobody is viewing Channel 8, Suria, Vasantham or CNA, there is no use in funding SMT or Mediacorp.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is precisely because people are reading, viewing and hearing our mainstream media that they deserve to be supported.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is because the public see them as trusted sources of news that we must do all we can to keep them as viable propositions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As can be seen also through the KPIs set by MCI, the Government's key interest is to ensure the reach of SMT's products.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: No one gains if these products lack credibility and are ignored by audiences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the contrary, we are funding them precisely because they do have readers who trust them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MCI will work closely with SMT to ensure that our local news media upholds quality journalism delivered in innovative and engaging ways.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One, in terms of access to future print copies of the newspaper.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I remember fondly riding in my father's car, rolling down the manual window and shouting out in dialect "ma biew po" and exchanging a couple of coins for a copy of the evening tabloid.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of our older generation continue to rely on access to news via the printed copies.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this restructuring and the pivot towards digital, how will the Government ensure the continued availability of printed copies in the future so that our elders in society are not left out?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Two, in terms of the workforce in SMT.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Over the last few years, I recall that in October 2009, there was a restructuring and 70 staff from SPH's Media Group were laid off.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And I think in 2020, a further 5% of the workforce, over 100, were also laid off as part of addressing the challenges of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As it continues to pivot and transform itself, how will the Government, through its funding mechanism, ensure that workers within the Media Group are fairly treated as it continues to pivot towards the digital sphere?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On his question about access to print, both the Government and SMT are very mindful that significant segments of our population rely on print to read about the daily happenings in Singapore and to get a perspective of the issues that are of importance to us.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, retaining the availability of print will remain a priority for quite a while, I believe.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The key issue is how SMT can do this in a way that is still efficient and does not drain its resources unnecessarily.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I can give Mr Alex Yam that assurance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The best thing I think we can do to retain talents within SMT is to provide them with the support to make that transformation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Talents everywhere, including journalistic talents in media companies, want to know that they have a future.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is the main reason that they will stay on, invest their time and effort to produce quality journalism.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And the only way we can do so is if the digital transformation is not a start-stop process, not a half-hearted process, but one that is taken with great commitment and passion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is what energises them and this is what makes them want to stay.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At this present moment, as it turns out, there is intense competition for talent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, SMT and, actually, all media companies, are working very hard to keep as many talent as possible.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Against this backdrop, it would be most unwise if SMT or any other media company were to be perceived by their employees of unfair treatment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is in their own interest to ensure that they paint a realistic vision of the future and they commit the resources to help their talent grow and develop along with the organisation's transformation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I have confidence in SMT that they are minded to look after their people because they are committed to the public to provide quality journalism, which cannot be achieved without the talent within their vault.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Minister, with close to $1 billion of Government funding for SMT committed over the next five years, how will the Government assure Singaporeans that SMT's content will not be tainted by allegations of political interference?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I want to emphasise this: up to $180 million dollars.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am actually not so surprised that Mr Pritam Singh put this question up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if I may, Mr Pritam Singh's question, again asking about influence on editors, journalist, is too predictable, if I may put it this way.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: His question seems to suggest that he does not trust the journalists and our mainstream media to be objective in reporting, to apply their minds and to be discerning or to have a sense of responsibility to truthful reporting for the public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hope I am wrong in thinking that this is what Mr Pritam Singh is suggesting, but that is what came to mind when he spoke those words.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Regardless of what I say or what Mr Pritam Singh may suggest, the true test is whether the public trusts the media and how they exercise their choice on a day-to-day basis in consuming news media, when so many alternatives are available to them at zero cost.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And, fortunately for us, for all of us, our local mainstream media are trusted by people and we have every reason to keep it so.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have filed a Parliamentary Question in relation to women and tech.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am very heartened to also find out recently that SMT has appointed a female CEO with vast experience in the IT industry to lead the organisation in this transformation.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is just a suggestion which I wish to put across to the Ministry to urge SMT to take into consideration that, in this transformation, they can be a very good and leading role model to encourage more women to enter, stay and progress with the organisation in this challenging yet meaningful journey.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will be more than happy to convey it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think, looking at the leadership of SMT all the way from its Chairman to its CEO and its senior team, I have no doubt that they are open to all kinds of talent, whether they are men or women, and they will do everything they can to hold as many of them in this organisation and help to propel its forward transformation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may just quickly follow up with the question for Minister Josephine Teo.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is the readers voting with their hands when they swipe their mobile phones on the screen and giving that demonstration of confidence in our local mainstream media through the reach and engagement data that is publicly available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not me claiming that the local mainstream media is trusted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are asked these questions through surveys conducted by institutions that have good standing; I mentioned the Reuters Institute.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They did not give this response to a question that I put to them; this is an independent survey done by a respected organisation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the facts speak for themselves and it is not for us to speculate why.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I think what Assoc Prof Jamus Lim is trying to say is that, if they trust these local mainstream media so much, why are they not buying or paying for subscription?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if they were doing so, then the local mainstream media would not have to turn to the Government for funding support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I thought that in my earlier responses to Members' questions, I had made it quite clear that this situation for print media companies is not unique to SMT.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And without advertising revenue, these media outlets and companies will be loss-making.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Guardian's example is a very stark one.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is not just your ability to reach audiences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The audiences can get news content free of charge almost anywhere.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not have to pay to get news, but we will choose where we spend our time, in order to get trusted news.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And that is what is the most important of all and that is why our local mainstream media deserve to be supported.
